Title: Stolen Renoir paintings found behind wall in France
Article:
PARIS: Two paintings by impressionist master Pierre-Auguste Renoir, stolen from a museum in southern France and later discovered hidden behind a wall, have sustained slight damage, prosecutors said on Monday.
In September, thieves broke into the museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer and escaped with two works by Renoir, abandoning two others as they fled.
The value of all four paintings had been estimated at nine million euros ($10 million).
On Friday, authorities announced that the two outstanding stolen works had been found.
They were a portrait titled "Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano" and a depiction of a woman at a well called "Young Woman at the Well."
Speaking to reporters in Paris, Marseille prosecutor Nicolas Bessone said the paintings were recovered last Thursday during a search of a home in the southern town of Clermont-l'Herault.
The discovery of the stolen works followed the arrest of six people, including a woman, last Wednesday, said Bessone.
"The paintings were hidden behind a solid cinderblock wall. They were completely undetectable," Bessone said.
"It was through interrogation work that investigators were able to get the receiver of the stolen goods to admit that he had indeed taken possession of the paintings."
A 29-year-old man seen as the main suspect was charged at the weekend after DNA evidence linked him to the theft.
The two paintings were "in relatively good condition", although "the two works showed signs of damage," Bessone said, speaking alongside the head of France's national judicial police, Christian Sainte.
The frame of "Young Woman at the Well" was slightly damaged, while "the canvas of 'Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano' had a tear," Bessone said.
The tear was located "on the dress" in the portrait, the prosecutor said, adding that both paintings "will require restoration work."
LATEST HEIST
Culture Minister Catherine Pegard praised "the efficiency and determination of all those who made this outcome possible."
"Their commitment made it possible to recover these works in record time," the culture ministry said.
A spate of heists at French museums – including at the Louvre – has highlighted inadequate security in some cases and led to questions about whether criminal gangs see them as soft targets.
Crown jewels valued at around $100 million were stolen in broad daylight from the Louvre in Paris last year.
While the four suspected Louvre robbers were arrested, the jewels they are accused of grabbing in the seven-minute heist have still not been found.

Title: Influencers should not exploit 3R issues for social media content - Yuneswaran
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Social media influencers have been reminded not to exploit issues involving race, religion and royalty (3R), particularly religious rituals, for online content, in the interest of preserving harmony in the country's multiracial society.
Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said influencers with large followings should be more responsible in producing content and spreading positive values instead of playing on 3R sentiments.
"If possible, stay away from issues involving 3R, as influencers may not know about the religious rituals or customs of certain communities, especially if they do not profess that religion.
"We have many positive things that can be promoted together with the National Unity Ministry," he said when met after attending Bernama TV's Ruang Bicara programme at Wisma Bernama today.
He was commenting on a viral issue involving an influencer believed to have participated in a religious ceremony during the Thaipusam celebration at Batu Caves, Selangor.
Yuneswaran said the ministry viewed the issue involving religious rituals seriously and hoped it would be handled tactfully, adding that the investigation had been left entirely to the religious authorities and the police.
He also urged the public not to rush to judgement or politicise the issue, but to allow the authorities to conduct their investigation and resolve the matter promptly.
In addition, he invited social media influencers to work with the ministry to promote the Federal Constitution, the Rukun Negara and the National Nationhood Programme.
"Under the ministry, we recommend that these issues (3R) be avoided. Although our society comprises people of various races and ethnic groups, we can attend various ceremonies, events and celebrations; however, when rituals are involved, I hope they will be respected," he said.
Yesterday, the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) confirmed that it had begun investigating a viral post involving an individual believed to be Muslim who was alleged to have participated in another religion's ritual in contravention of Islamic law. – BERNAMA

Title: 2027 Budget: Govt confident of RM510bil expenditure without introducing new taxes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is confident it can fund the RM510 billion expenditure under the 2027 Budget without introducing new taxes, says Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said the government was prioritising better governance to curb leakages and wastage, and improve the efficiency of public spending.
"The government's approach is to ensure that what we spend is money well spent to improve the country's economy and for the people's benefit.
"When we have focus and carry out our responsibilities well, the government and the country will be more successful in the future," he said on RTM 1's Bicara Naratif programme today.
The programme was titled 'Budget 2027: Reaching For The Skies, While Anchored on Our Values'.
Amir Hamzah said Malaysia's strengthening economic data reflected foreign investors' confidence in the country, which could help generate national income.
"But the most important thing is ensuring that when the revenue is there, we spend wisely, we close the gaps for any leakages that occur, and we increase the returns we get more efficiently in government expenditure, and this will be tied to the introduction of several new laws," he said.

Title: Nepal rescuers search for missing after flash flood
Article:
KATHMANDU: Nepali rescuers searched for five missing people on Monday, a day after devastating flash floods swept away more than 200 houses and five bridges along the Budhi Gandaki river.
Videos showed a dark, debris-filled river surging through the hills in central Nepal's Gorkha district.
No deaths have been confirmed.
On Sunday, 95 people including nine foreigners were rescued.
"We are continuing our work on rescue and relief," Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal Army spokesman told AFP, adding that four helicopters had been deployed.
"We do not have any new information on the five missing," he added.
About 150 foreign trekkers are in the area, according to the Trekking Agencies' Association of Nepal, many on the popular Manaslu circuit trek.
"We are working with authorities to rescue those who are stranded because of the roads," the association's president Sagar Pandey said.
Authorities were also delivering aid to affected communities, with many residents fleeing their homes on Sunday morning as the torrent hit.
The flood also struck hydropower plants, according to the national disaster agency.
"I screamed out loud to get people out. Just a few minutes after people ran out the flood crashed through," local resident Indra Bahadur Gurung said.
"We have always lived here, and find it difficult to leave. I hope the government will manage something safe for us soon."
'REDUCING FUTURE RISKS'
Preliminary data suggests that a landslide had dammed the river. It then burst, with the water surging downstream.
"The government has already begun taking the necessary steps to restore normal life," Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a post on social media late Sunday.
He urged residents to stay in safe locations and to avoid travel on risky roads and bridges.
Nepal is still recovering from devastating floods on August 26, triggered by a mountain glacial collapse, which killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing.
Shah told the United Nations last month that the August flooding "was a warning to the world" about the rising dangers of climate change.
Basanta Raj Adhikari, director at the Centre for Disaster Studies at Tribhuvan University, said that the latest flood showed the need for better monitoring.
"The frequency of the disasters is dangerous... it shows we need to go beyond our traditional river-level based early warning systems," Adhikari said, suggesting satellite images and seismometers could help detect events earlier.
The Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said Sunday that the floods highlighted the "range of hazards capable of generating destructive floods" in Himalayan river systems.
"Understanding what triggered this flood will be critical for reducing future risks and strengthening resilience," the centre's director general Pema Gyamtsho said in the statement.
Heavy rainfall in late September also triggered floods and landslides, killing at least 21 people, according to the disaster agency.

Title: MoH to recommend permanent posts for contract dental, pharmacy officers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry (MoH) will recommend absorbing contract dental and pharmacy officers into permanent positions for the consideration Finance Ministry and the cabinet.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the proposal would be pursued within a reasonable timeframe, based on the approach previously used to address the issue of contract medical doctors.
"...the first step will be followed by other service schemes, namely dentists and pharmacists as well," he said when met after appearing as a guest on Bernama TV's Ruang Bicara programme titled 'Realising Budget 2027 With the Health Minister'.
He said the recruitment of dental and pharmacy officers into permanent positions would utilise a new quota separate from the 9,000 permanent medical doctor positions announced under the 2027 Budget.
The Malaysian Dental Association (MDA) previously have urged the government and MoH to consider permanent appointments for contract dental officers, following the announcement of permanent appointments for medical doctors.
Commenting on reports regarding dental officers whose contracts ended without being renewed, Dzulkefly said MoH would continue to pay attention to their welfare and work experience within the public healthcare system.
In another development, Dzulkefly expressed hope that MoF would consider a request for an initial allocation of about RM100 million to strengthen the management of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) at the primary healthcare level.
He said the allocation was crucial to enhance prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, and continuous control of chronic diseases such as diabetes and high blood pressure.
"Matters related to NCD management are a major component that I am bringing into the reforms. In addition to PeKa B40, which received an allocation of RM80 million, managing NCDs from a healthcare perspective is essential to effectively address this chronic disease pandemic.
"It encompasses not only first-stage screening, but also continuous diagnosis, treatment, and control for conditions such as diabetes and high blood pressure," he said.
He added that the ministry's benchmarking of per capita spending on NCD management took into account practices in countries such as Singapore and Indonesia, as well as global trends prioritising primary healthcare services.

Title: Indonesia rules out national disaster status for forest fires for now
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia will not declare its prolonged forest and land fires a national disaster for now, saying it remains capable of managing the crisis despite concerns over transboundary haze affecting neighbouring countries, including Malaysia.
Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs Dudung Abdurachman said the decision was made at a limited cabinet meeting chaired by President Prabowo Subianto at the Presidential Palace here on Monday.
"Not yet, not yet. We are still capable of handling it," he told reporters after the meeting.
Dudung said offers of international assistance were not discussed, although he acknowledged concerns from neighbouring countries over the haze.
"There have indeed been responses from other countries regarding these forest fires, but we have made maximum efforts," he said, expressing hope that the situation could be resolved soon.
On Oct 8, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had contacted Prabowo about the haze and conveyed Malaysia's readiness to help to combat the fires.
Meanwhile, Dudung said Prabowo had directed firefighting efforts to focus on Tanjung Puting National Park and other affected areas in Central Kalimantan, as well as South Sumatra.
"Tanjung Puting and areas surrounding the national park must be protected because there is wildlife there," he said.
The park is internationally known for its orangutan conservation and rehabilitation programmes.
Earlier today, House of Representatives Commission IV member Daniel Johan has urged the government to declare the prolonged forest and land fires a national disaster and remain open to international assistance, including Malaysia's offer of firefighting support.
Daniel said the scale of the crisis required regional cooperation and that accepting foreign help should not be viewed as a sign of weakness.
Meanwhile, Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni warned that authorities must remain on high alert for another month, with natural rainfall not expected in parts of Indonesia until mid-November or even December.
During an inspection of firefighting operations at the Liang Anggang Protected Forest in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan, he said the government was preparing to suspend or revoke the business permits of another five or six companies over fire-related violations.
Action had been taken against 26 companies, including five forestry concession holders in Kalimantan whose permits were revoked on Sept 21, he said.
The concession covered about  92,464 hectares, of which approximately 1,169 hectares had been affected by fires.

Title: Sinkhole-prone areas must be assessed before development approval, says ministry
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Technical assessments and inspections of aging utilities in sinkhole-prone areas must be conducted before local authorities approve any development, the Housing and Local Government Ministry said.
The ministry said the decision was made at the 51st National Physical Planning Council (NPPC) meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
"This approach is crucial to ensure public safety and geological risks are addressed from the early stages of development planning," the ministry said in a statement.
The ministry said NPPC also urged state governments to improve the provision of quality public open spaces and expedite their gazettement to ensure public access to safe and comfortable recreational areas, while promoting healthy lifestyles and strengthening community interaction.
It also approved the Fifth National Physical Plan (RFN5) and the Third National Urbanisation Policy (DPN3) as strategic frameworks for the country's physical and urban development.
RFN5 is the country's highest-level spatial planning document, covering Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Labuan until 2040. It focuses on sustainable land use, natural resource conservation and greater resilience to climate change and disasters.
Its targets include implementing smart city initiatives across 115 local authorities, maintaining at least 50 per cent forest cover and providing 1.6 million hectares of potential land to support economic growth.
DPN3, which runs until 2035, covers 203 cities under 101 local authorities in Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan. It aims to ensure urban growth is planned in a more structured, inclusive and sustainable manner, taking into account demographic, economic and technological changes, as well as climate change challenges.
The ministry said the council also considered the Putrajaya Structure Plan 2050 draft, which outlines the development direction for the national administrative centre.
The plan includes a target population of 305,000, the provision of 83,438 housing units, achieving carbon neutrality and the use of artificial intelligence in urban management.
The meeting also agreed to the Perlis State Structure Plan 2040, which outlines development strategies including the Perlis Inland Port, the Chuping Valley Industrial Area and the strengthening of the state's granary areas.
"Overall, the decisions of the 51st NPPC reinforce the government's commitment to ensuring the country's physical and urban development is planned, sustainable, inclusive, resilient and responsive to future changes, in line with the Malaysia Madani aspirations," the ministry said.

Title: NST Leader: Disaster alert system faces litmus test, success hinges on public response
Article:
ON Nov 19, expect a special government text message  to pop out of your handphone screens. The message may "warn" you of an impending "natural disaster" near your area or residence.
You might also be advised to "immediately evacuate" your homes and proceed to the nearest shelter. Don't be alarmed: the message is a test from the Cell Broadcast System (CBS), a national disaster warning system that is undergoing pilot  testing.
Developed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, the CBS transmits disaster alerts directly to handphones in affected areas.
Circumventing  handphone numbers, SMS  or Internet connection, the CBS will soon replace the existing SMS-based disaster warning system to provide faster and precise alerts.
As of 2025, the United Nations reported that 44 countries  have adopted mobile-based public warning systems for earthquakes, tsunamis, floods, wildfires, severe storms and other emergencies.   Malaysia's current system transmits targeted flood-warning SMS through the National Disaster Management Agency and telecommunications companies.
The CBS is technically sound, able to improve the speed in issuing alerts on emergencies.
The key issue  is whether the government can connect hazard monitoring, accurate location targeting, telecommunications networks and clear instructions into a single and reliable national warning system.
From a technical standpoint, the CBS technology can blast an alert to all compatible handphones rather than send individual messages.
While the CBS can penetrate heavy voice and data traffic, it still depends on functioning mobile network infrastructure, though no special app is required.    The challenge is rural coverage, raising public trust and awareness, and backup distribution methods in areas with poor coverage.
The CBS must also be able to send alerts in Bahasa Malaysia and English, and local dialects when necessary, while clearly distinguishing between advisories, imminent threats and evacuation orders.
The CBS should also accommodate individuals with visual, hearing or reading disabilities,  which may require tailored video messages or other formats.
The Nov 19 pilot may launch in high-risk areas, such as flood-prone parts of Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Kelantan and Pahang.
Malaysians  know that skies can be  clear and sunny and rivers  calm, but floods can strike rapidly, making the CBS crucial for  delivering timely warnings.  The value of the CBS lies in its targeted warnings, giving families precious minutes to seek shelter, help vulnerable residents and allow authorities to respond effectively.
The CBS must complement a culture of preparedness rather than create a false sense of security as its usefulness depends on reception, understanding and action.
Ultimately, the CBS should not be judged by daily emergencies but by whether we are ready to act when  disasters strike.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five Malaysians held in Japan over RM3.1mil cocaine haul hidden in shoes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Four men and a woman from Malaysia have been arrested at Haneda Airport in Tokyo, Japan, for attempting to smuggle about 5kg of cocaine worth 120 million yen (RM3.1 million), hidden beneath shoe insoles, on Saturday.
The group is believed to have brought the drugs from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) before their activities were uncovered during customs checks upon arrival in Japan.
According to Fuji News Network (FNN), customs officers became suspicious of one of the suspects because his shoes had unusually thick soles.
An initial inspection found cocaine hidden beneath the insoles of two suspects, prompting officers to identify three others believed to have travelled with them.
Tokyo Reporter, citing Nippon News Network (NNN), reported that the three others had also concealed cocaine using the same method.
TBS News DIG reported that each suspect had hidden about 1kg of cocaine, with 500g concealed beneath the insole of each shoe.
One of the five suspects, Mohamad Danial Farhan Abdul Rahman, 24, claimed he had been offered RM8,000 to transport drugs overseas through the Telegram messaging app.
He was also reportedly given a pair of shoes to conceal the drugs.
Meanwhile, NHK reported that four suspects admitted to the allegations during questioning, while a 25-year-old woman denied them.
The woman claimed she did not know that the package she was carrying contained cocaine.
Tokyo Metropolitan Police are investigating whether the group was recruited by a Malaysia-based criminal syndicate to carry out international drug smuggling.

Title: Man from KL dies after falling from Penang mall car park
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 47-year-old man from Kuala Lumpur died after falling from an upper-level car park at a shopping mall in Lebuh Teck Soon here tonight.
Northeast district police received a report about the incident around 9.10pm.
A witness reportedly saw the man fall from the car park.
Northeast district deputy police chief Superintendent Lee Swee Sake confirmed the incident.
"Preliminary investigations at the scene and an examination of the deceased's body found no elements of criminal activity," he said in a statement.
Lee said a sudden death report would be opened to facilitate further investigations.

Title: Malaysia seeks foreign expertise to unlock RM747bil rare earth potential
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is seeking greater foreign investment and technology transfers to develop its rare earth industry and tap mineral resources estimated to be worth RM747.2 billion.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said strategic partnerships with technologically advanced countries were needed to strengthen Malaysia's rare earth processing and manufacturing capabilities, particularly in high-value industries.
He said Malaysia had an estimated 16.2 million tonnes of non-radioactive rare earth resources, with industry development expected to create 4,000 jobs.
Johari said the government aimed to develop an integrated rare earth ecosystem covering the entire value chain, from mining and processing to finished product manufacturing.
"Malaysia needs to leverage strategic cooperation and technology transfers from partner countries with expertise in rare earth processing," he said in a parliamentary reply.
He said such cooperation would strengthen domestic capabilities and position Malaysia as a key player in the global critical minerals supply chain.
The approach was in line with the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 (NIMP 2030), which aims to strengthen the country's industrial capabilities and attract high-value investments, he added.
Citing existing investments, Johari said Australian-owned Lynas Malaysia Sdn Bhd had operated a rare earth processing facility in Gebeng, Pahang, since 2012.
Lynas invested RM3.8 billion in Malaysia between the 2008 and 2025 financial years, while contributing an estimated RM4.81 billion to the country's gross domestic product between 2013 and 2021, based on company information, he said.
Johari was responding to Datuk Ahmad Amzad Mohamed @ Hashim (PN-Kuala Terengganu), who asked about the government's position on Lynas's four-year rare earth supply arrangement with the United States Department of Defense and its implications for Malaysia's strategic interests.
On the agreement, Johari said Lynas had informed the government that it was a commercial arrangement managed by its American subsidiary, Lynas LLC USA.
He said the company indicated that the rare earth oxides were intended for research and development in the permanent magnet manufacturing industry.
Johari acknowledged that determining the ultimate use of rare earth materials was difficult because global supply chains were fragmented, with products frequently changing hands between manufacturers and suppliers.

Title: Iron and steel sector faces pressure from dumped imports
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The iron and steel sector is among the industries most frequently affected by dumped imports, with the government investigating products from six countries and territories to protect local manufacturers from unfair trade practices.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the investigations covered imports from China, Taipei, South Korea, Japan, India and Vietnam.
"These products are generally intermediate inputs in production chains rather than finished products or cheap consumer goods sold directly to consumers," he said in a written parliamentary reply.
The government amended the Countervailing and Anti-Dumping Duties Act in 2025 and is reviewing the regulations introduced in 1994 to ensure trade remedies remain relevant and effective.
Malaysia's total imports rose 22.4 per cent to RM1.158 trillion from January to August 2026, while imports from China increased 41.2 per cent to RM308.12 billion, accounting for 21.1 per cent of total imports.
Johari said the increase was driven mainly by intermediate and capital goods used for production and investment, which rose 15.6 per cent, while imports of consumer goods grew 3.7 per cent.
He said the government continued to monitor import prices and dumping trends, and would take action if investigations established injury to local industries or an import surge that met the criteria under domestic laws and WTO rules.
"If investigations establish injury or an import surge in accordance with domestic laws and WTO rules, trade remedies such as anti-dumping, countervailing or safeguard duties will be imposed," he said.
He was responding to a question from Mohd Syahir Sulaiman (PN-Bachok) on the impact of trade diversion and import dumping amid rising global tariffs, the sectors affected and measures to protect local industries.
The ministry had previously announced that an
anti-dumping investigation
was launched on Aug 6 following petitions from local steel manufacturers, who claimed that unfairly priced imports were harming the domestic industry.

Title: Search for man swept away in Kajang river suspended due to heavy rain
Article:
KAJANG: The search and rescue operation for a man believed to have been swept away by river currents in Sungai Chuah yesterday was suspended this afternoon following heavy rain.
The victim, an Indian man believed to be in his 40s, was last seen wearing a white shirt and drifting in the river near Jalan Pasir Emas 2 before disappearing.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 5.23pm yesterday after members of the public reported seeing the man being swept away.
He said firefighters from the Kajang Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene six minutes later and immediately launched a search for the missing man.
"Initial search efforts were concentrated along the riverbanks before the operation was expanded with the assistance of the Water Rescue Unit (PPDA) and K9 unit.
"Seven PPDA personnel arrived at the scene at 6.38pm, while a forward command post was established at 6.42pm to coordinate the search operation," he said.
Ashrul said rescue personnel continued searching the surrounding riverbanks until late last night, but the victim remained missing.
He said the operation entered its second day today, with rescuers deploying kayaks and boats to search the river while the K9 unit conducted searches along the riverbanks.
"Search efforts continued throughout the day, but operations had to be suspended at 4.30pm due to heavy rain at the location.
"The search and rescue operation will resume tomorrow," he said.
Ashrul said the operation involved 23 firefighters, five police personnel and two members of the Malaysian Volunteer Fire Brigade (RBM).
Firefighters from the Kajang, Shah Alam and Port Klang fire stations, including specialist water rescue personnel and the K9 unit, were mobilised for the operation.
As of this evening, the victim had yet to be located.
Earlier today, The Selangor Civil Defence Force (APM) said its Hulu Langat district office was informed of the incident around 7.26pm today.
However, preliminary information obtained from Kajang police indicated that the incident had occurred yesterday.
Following the notification, a team comprising four APM officers and five personnel was dispatched to the location to assist in the search operation.

Title: Takaichi's fiscal shift faces market test
Article:
JAPANESE Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration is ramping up efforts to shed its growth and easy money image through changes in rhetoric, a move that may backfire unless it is met with action such as substantial cuts to spending.
With major economies facing increased scrutiny from bond investors worried about rising inflation and yields, a lack of clarity on funding could cause another bond selloff in Japan given its US$7 trillion debt pile that is the biggest among advanced nations.
Takaichi vowed to cap new debt issuance around 40 trillion yen, even as spending requests for next year's budget hit a record 143 trillion yen.
A planned two-year sales tax cut would also cost roughly 4 trillion yen per year.
The government hopes to fill the gap by tapping rising tax revenues and state funds, a tricky task that would still pump money and inflationary pressures into the economy, analysts say.
"Markets look at the substance of policy and won't believe words alone," said Eiji Doke, chief bond strategist at SBI Securities.
"It's not that market players misunderstand Takaichi's policies. Rather, what they're watching is completely different from what the administration is trying to do."
Takaichi became premier in October last year with a pledge to ramp up spending to spur growth. She filled government panels with her reflationist aides to promote loose fiscal policy.
"Only by strengthening the economy would Japan achieve fiscal sustainability," she said in a policy speech back then in explaining her plan to compile a big spending package.
The administration's hefty fuel subsidies, a tax-cut pledge and big investment plans cemented market perceptions of its policies being reflationary as the economy struggled to recover from decades of low growth and low inflation.
But rising bond yields have become constraints on Takaichi's ambitions, forcing her administration to change its language.
"Fiscal sustainability is a prerequisite in pursuing our 'responsible and proactive' fiscal policy," she told Parliament last Monday.
She also pledged to "control" bond issuance and enhance communication with markets in a sign of the administration's sensitivity to rising Japanese government bond (JGB) yields.
The benchmark 10-year JGB yield has hit multi-decade highs on concern Takaichi's spending plans may lead to increased debt issuance and strain Japan's worsening finances.
Efforts to phase out the administration's reflationist image geared up after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's calls in August for Japan to depart from Abenomics — a mix of loose fiscal and monetary steps deployed by former premier Shinzo Abe to beat deflation.
Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama led the communication shift.
In a recent media interview, she said the government decided around late August to recalibrate its messaging to reassure markets Takaichi was not pursuing reflationary policies.
Soon after, reflationist aides began to change tone.
Economy Minister Minoru Kiuchi, for one, said on Sept 25 that the phase of Abenomics-style reflationary policies was over.
Former Bank of Japan (BOJ) deputy governor Masazumi Wakatabe, who also sits on a government panel, also said last month reflationist policies "have no place in Japan now".
The shift in tone occurred at the BOJ, too.
Ayano Sato, a reflationist board member picked by Takaichi, told Kyodo News on Wednesday that she supports raising rates.
The government began to stress its spending plans are aimed at boosting supply capacity rather than reflating growth.
Markets are focusing on whether Takaichi will meet words with action as the government drafts next fiscal year's budget.
Katayama vowed to tap unused funds and identify wasteful spending to seek revenues under Japan's equivalent of the US Department of Government Efficiency initiative, focusing on the 7 trillion yen pooled by about 200 state funds.
But tapping such funds for spending is unsustainable and could stimulate the economy, running counter to the BOJ's efforts to curb inflation with rate hikes, some analysts say.
Former BOJ board member Asahi Noguchi, known as a reflationist, said now was the time to avoid boosting demand and causing bond yield rises that crowd out private investment.
"The administration probably didn't have a coherent view, with some clinging to the legacy of Abenomics, though that seems to have changed," he said.
"The key is to cut wasteful spending and convince markets Japan is serious about fiscal reform."
The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Vance 2028 buzz growing, but midterms could sting
Article:
THE message was clear as United States Vice-President JD Vance shook hands in his native Ohio with a woman wearing a "Vance 2028" cap — at least from his supporter's perspective.
Donald Trump's deputy has yet to declare that he will run for the White House in two years' time. But what was supposed to be a campaign rally on Friday for Republican candidates in November's US midterm elections in Lima, Ohio, looked a lot more like a Vance rally.
With a theatrical flourish, Vance descended from the steps of Air Force Two, the vice-presidential jet, and received a rapturous reception as he entered the event in a flag-draped airport hangar.
"Man, it feels good to be home," Vance said to cheers.
Unusually for Vance on the campaign trail, he then went down to greet the crowd in person — shaking hands, patting arms and meeting the lady with the black pro-Vance hat.
There's just one problem for Vance: the midterms themselves.
Polls show Trump's unpopularity, the Iran war and the price of living could cost Republicans their majority in Congress.
And Ohio, which voted for Trump in the last three presidential elections, has turned from a stronghold into one of the tightest electoral battlegrounds for the Nov 3 vote.
There are nail-biting races for Vance's old senate seat, currently held by Jon Husted, and for the governorship of Ohio, where former Republican presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy is standing.
In a sign of Republican concerns, Vance's visit comes days after Trump travelled to the state and the 80-year-old president is due back there next week.
For Trump, losing control of Congress could mean he spends his last two years in office battling multiple Democrat-led investigations.
For Vance, losing Ohio could seriously damage a political brand that was largely built on the blue-collar roots in the state described in his bestselling memoir "Hillbilly Elegy".
"I think it has nothing to do with 2028," he insisted to reporters when asked how important it was to win Ohio for Republicans as he looked to a presidential run. "It has to do with how we're going to govern our country over the next two years, the next 10 years."
Despite Vance's comments, the race for 2028 will effectively start the day after the midterms.
While Vance is widely considered the frontrunner to be Trump's heir, he's made no announcement yet and it's far from a done deal.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said he won't run against Vance, but his speech on western civilisation against the backdrop of the Acropolis in Athens was widely seen as a pitch for the job.
There is a growing buzz around the youthful vice-president.
Like any good candidate, Vance is increasingly bringing his family on the stump.
The 42-year-old took his wife Usha, three of their four children and their dog Atlas on Air Force Two for the flight to Cincinnati, where Vance cast an early vote for the midterms.
Vance is also raising money. His role as the finance chair of the Republican National Committee puts him at the centre of a nexus of wealthy donors.
Politically, Vance is quietly trying to exorcise the vice-president's curse of being tied to the policies of the outgoing president — one that Kamala Harris suffered from in 2024.
His speeches have subtly positioned him as more conscious of the financial woes of US families, even as Trump dismisses what he calls the "affordability hoax".
Staking out his own positions also helps counter the idea that Vance is a political shape-shifter — he once compared Trump to Hitler before becoming his vice-president.
The recent Catholic convert on Friday sought to distance himself from another key administration figure, Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth, over the announcement that a US military firing squad execution would be livestreamed.
"I've seen these announcements. I don't know that that's going to happen," Vance told a reporter travelling with him on Friday, adding that if it was going to be "through livestream, I'm not going to be watching it".
The writer is from AFP

Title: Cybercrime Act expected to come into force in early 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Cybercrime Act is expected to come into force in early 2027 as the government steps up efforts to tackle increasingly complex and organised online scams.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the legal framework had been strengthened through amendments to the Penal Code, introducing Sections 424A, 424B, 424C(1) and 424C(2), and the Criminal Procedure Code, through Section 116D.
Action against online crime is also supported by provisions under the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and the Online Safety Act 2025, which aims to improve online safety and protect users from harmful content and risks.
"The legal framework on cybercrime has also been strengthened through the introduction of the Cybercrime Bill, in line with technological developments and the changing landscape of cybercrime threats.
"The Cybercrime Act is expected to come into force in early 2027," he said in a written parliamentary reply.
Saifuddin said the Home Ministry would continue to review existing laws to ensure they remained relevant and effective in addressing evolving cybercrime threats.
"The Home Ministry will continue to review and assess the need to improve existing legal provisions from time to time to ensure the country's legal framework remains relevant and effective in addressing the growing threat of cybercrime," he said.
He was responding to Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu), who asked whether the government would amend outdated laws and impose heavier penalties, including caning, on scammers following RM2.97 billion in cybercrime losses recorded in 2025.
The Dewan Rakyat passed the
Cybercrime Bill 2026
on July 1.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had said the legislation included safeguards against abuse, with investigative powers subject to checks and balances and established legal procedures.

Title: 'Ziad's body was smoking': Cousin recounts lightning strike that killed Pasir Mas student
Article:
PASIR MAS: A Form Two student's body appeared to be smoking after he was struck by lightning while fishing in a padi field in Kampung Tasek Berangan here around 4.30pm today, his cousin recalled.
"When the lightning struck, all four of us fell backwards, and at that moment, I saw Ziad's body smoking," said Haziq Qayyum Rosli, 12.
Haziq is the cousin of Muhammad Ziad Zikri Abdul Hadi, who was killed in the incident.
Haziq, who sustained an injury to the back of his right shoulder, said they were walking towards their motorcycles to return home due to sudden heavy rain when the incident happened.
"We arrived at the padi field at 4pm. But it suddenly rained and I asked Ziad and our other friend if we could go home because I was worried the rain would get heavier. At that time, there was no lightning yet.
"However, Ziad asked us to be patient as we had just arrived and he had already caught two fish, so he still wanted to continue fishing.
"At that moment (when lightning striked), I saw Ziad's body smoking, and we ran home to inform Ziad's father," he said when met here.
Haziq said he initially thought Ziad had only fainted, before others arrived and told them that he had died.
"The four of us liked fishing at that spot and never expected this to happen.
"I am very sad because the four of us were so close," he said.
Earlier, Ziad's father,
Abdul Hadi Abdul Ghani, 60,
said he rushed to the padi field and cradled his son after learning that the boy had been struck by lightning, only to find that he was already dead.
Recounting the incident, Hadi said he had been asleep at home when his youngest of five children went fishing with a friend and cousin.
Ziad was a student at SMK Sri Kiambang here. His body is expected to be buried tomorrow morning.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wan Rosdy advises Pahang residents to take precautions as haze worsens
Article:
KUANTAN: Pahang residents have been advised to limit outdoor activities, avoid open burning and wear face masks as the haze worsens.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said high-risk groups, including children, the elderly and those with respiratory problems, should take extra precautions.
"Parents and event organisers must take appropriate measures to minimise exposure to unhealthy air.
"Those experiencing symptoms should seek medical attention at the nearest healthcare facility without delay," he said in a statement.
Wan Rosdy said he was aware that the Pahang Education Department had ordered
schools in Kuantan and Rompin
to close tomorrow due to worsening haze and prevailing Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
"The decision was made to safeguard the safety, health and well-being of students, teachers and the entire education community.
"The state government will continue to monitor developments closely with relevant agencies to ensure appropriate measures are taken in the people's best interests," he said.
Two air quality monitoring stations in Pahang recorded unhealthy air quality at 10pm today, with Balok Baru in Kuantan registering an API reading of 159 and Rompin recording 153.

Title: University student, retired engineer lose over RM690,000 to scams in Pahang
Article:
KUANTAN: A university student lost RM32,115 after being duped by a scammer posing as a police officer who accused him of money laundering.
Acting Bentong police chief Deputy Superintendent Azmi Mahmod said the 18-year-old victim handed over cash and jewellery worth more than RM32,000 to a woman near a supermarket in Karak, Bentong.
He said the incident occurred on Oct 7, when the student received a phone call from someone claiming to be a police officer who accused him of involvement in money laundering.
"The suspect threatened to arrest the victim if he did not follow instructions, causing him to panic and hand over cash and jewellery belonging to his parents to settle the case," he said in a statement.
Azmi said the victim handed the items to a masked woman and was told not to inform his family or anyone else.
He said police arrested a 21-year-old local woman near the supermarket around 6.20pm last Saturday.
"Investigations revealed that the female suspect had been offered a job by the syndicate, which claimed she had been appointed as a member of the 'Police Special Actions Unit'.
"She was instructed to collect the cash and jewellery from the victim before handing them over to a third party arranged by the syndicate," he said.
Azmi said investigations were ongoing to determine the suspect's role and identify others involved.
In a separate case, Bera police chief Superintendent Zulkiflee Nazir said a retired engineer lost RM660,000 in a fraudulent stock investment scheme.
He said the 56-year-old victim received a WhatsApp message from an unknown individual on Feb 5 offering an investment scheme with a minimum entry of RM10,000 and a promised return of 10 per cent.
"Believing the offer, the victim invested RM660,000 in seven transactions into three bank accounts under different company names.
"The victim received no returns as promised and realised he had been scammed when he was repeatedly asked to deposit more money," he said.
Police are investigating both cases under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.

Title: Father rushes to paddy field, finds son dead after lightning strike in Pasir Mas [WATCH]
Article:
PASIR MAS: A father rushed to a paddy field and cradled his 14-year-old son after learning that the boy had been struck by lightning, only to find that he was already dead.
"When I was told that Ziad had been struck by lightning, I rushed to the paddy field and cradled him, but my son was already dead," said Abdul Hadi Abdul Ghani, 60.
His son, Muhammad Ziad Zikri, a Form Two student, was killed by lightning while fishing at a paddy field in Kampung Tasek Berangan at 4.30pm today.
Recounting the incident, Hadi said he had been asleep at home when his youngest of five children went fishing with a friend and cousin.
"I was shocked when my nephew, who was fishing with Ziad, ran home and told me that my son had been struck by lightning.
"We rushed to the scene, about two kilometres from our house. By then, my other children had arrived and were trying to wake Ziad, thinking he had only fainted.
"I cradled Ziad, but he was already gone. We took him to Pasir Mas Hospital to confirm his death," he told reporters at his home tonight.
He said the incident was a shock as Ziad had left home at 4pm in good health, only to be brought home lifeless.
"Although we are grieving, we accept what happened as Allah's will.
"Ziad was a very good and obedient son. He was cheerful and always willing to help the family.
"His favourite pastimes were fishing and catching birds every evening," he said.
Ziad was a student at SMK Sri Kiambang here. Hadi said his son had attended school as usual and gone to his Quran class before heading out to fish.
"Last night, we talked and I reminded Ziad to attend his Quran classes regularly as preparation for the hereafter.
"He used to attend the classes occasionally and needed to be reminded, but today he went without being told after returning from school," he said.
Ziad's body is expected to be buried tomorrow morning.

Title: Foreigner filmed couple, threatened woman before raping her inside mall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracking down a foreigner, believed to be a Bangladeshi, who allegedly raped a woman on the seventh floor of a shopping centre near Jalan Cochrane here.
The incident is believed to have occurred about 7pm last Saturday, when the woman, in her 20s, was engaged in a sexual act with her boyfriend.
The suspect reportedly filmed the couple and threatened to circulate the footage if the woman refused to follow his instructions.
He then ordered the woman's boyfriend to leave before raping her.

Title: Foetus found at rubbish disposal site in One Selayang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A foetus believed to be about 24 weeks old was found at a rubbish disposal site in Jalan OS 1/4, One Selayang, Batu Caves, yesterday.
Gombak police chief Assistant Commissioner Ibrahim Husin said members of the public alerted police to the discovery at 7.20 pm.
He said police are investigating the case under Section 318 of the Penal Code, which concerns concealing a birth by secretly disposing of the body of a child who died before, during or after birth.
"If convicted, the offender faces up to two years in prison, a fine, or both," he said in a statement.
Ibrahim urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the Gombak police headquarters control centre at 03-6126 2222, investigating officer Inspector Prakash Sithambaram on 012-294 0827, or their nearest police station.

Title: Malaysia, Jordan explore high-tech cooperation to develop engineers – Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Jordan are exploring stronger cooperation in high-tech industries, particularly semiconductors and advanced technical education, to develop more engineers and skilled workers for future industry needs.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was among the key areas discussed during his meeting with Jordan's King Abdullah II, who was on a two-day state visit to Malaysia at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
Anwar said the talks also covered cooperation in higher education, skilled human capital development, emerging technologies and the semiconductor ecosystem.
"We also discussed potential cooperation in developing advanced technical education and training centres, including producing more engineers and skilled workers to meet future industry demands," he said on Facebook.
Anwar said discussions also covered expanding trade and investment, including a potential free trade agreement (FTA), tariff restructuring, stronger supply chains and cooperation in energy, transport, the halal industry and tourism.
Anwar said he and King Abdullah also exchanged views on geopolitical developments in West Asia, particularly in Palestine and Syria, and their implications for regional security and stability.
He said they also agreed on the urgent need to end atrocities against Palestinians, including continued violence and rights violations in Jerusalem and the West Bank.
"I stressed that Malaysia will remain steadfast in championing Palestinian rights while strengthening humanitarian assistance, particularly for the people of Gaza," he said.
Anwar said the Jordanian monarch also expressed appreciation for Malaysia's stance and efforts in supporting the Palestinian cause.
Anwar also expressed hope that the meeting would elevate Malaysia-Jordan relations through closer economic and technological cooperation, as well as shared commitments to humanity, peace and global justice.
The state visit was King Abdullah's second to Malaysia since May 2008, as both countries marked more than six decades of diplomatic relations established in 1965.
Prior to his departure after concluding the visit, King Abdullah granted Anwar an audience at the Bunga Raya Complex, Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), for about 30 minutes to discuss strengthening longstanding bilateral relations.
Bilateral trade reached RM993.4 million in 2025, up 15.2 per cent from 2024, while trade from January to August 2026 rose eight per cent year-on-year to RM740.7 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Semantan Estate files new suit seeking sale of RM13bil Duta Enclave land
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd and its liquidator have filed a new suit in the High Court here against the government and six other defendants over the Duta Enclave land in Kuala Lumpur.
They are seeking an order compelling the government to sell the land and account for the proceeds or, alternatively, pay equitable compensation.
The suit was filed on Oct 8 by Semantan Estate and its liquidator, Dr Lai Chee Chuen, through Messrs AG Kalidas Doris & Nada. The defendants are the government, the Federal Lands Commissioner, the minister responsible for land in the Federal Territories, the Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability, the director-general of Lands and Mines, the director of Lands and Mines (Federal Territories) and the Registrar of Titles (Federal Territories).
In its statement of claim, the company, which is in members' voluntary liquidation, estimated the land's current market value at between RM12 billion and RM13 billion. It alleged that the government had continued to occupy, develop and benefit from the land despite a 2009 High Court order declaring the purported acquisition "void ab initio" (void from the beginning).
Semantan Estate claimed that the government took possession of the land between 1956 and 1958 under the Land Acquisition Enactment 1923 for the stated purpose of establishing a "Diplomatic Enclave". The land was then divided into 38 lots measuring 230.851 acres (93.42 hectares), with the title registered under the Federal Lands Commissioner. The remaining 32.421 acres (13.12 hectares) were used for roads and infrastructure.
The plaintiffs also claimed that the land was never used for its gazetted purpose but was instead developed for official, cultural and commercial buildings, as well as roads, a flyover and other infrastructure.
The plaintiffs are seeking a declaration that the government holds the land on trust for Semantan Estate and an order compelling the government to sell it and account for the proceeds after permitted deductions.
Alternatively, they are seeking equitable compensation for the alleged breach of trust or damages under Article 13 of the Federal Constitution for the alleged deprivation of the company's property rights.
They are also seeking restitution for benefits allegedly derived by the government from its continued occupation and use of the land, interest at five per cent per annum on any sums ordered to be paid, costs and any other relief deemed fit by the court.
The court's e-filing system showed that the suit had been fixed for case management before High Court Judge Datuk Anand Ponnudurai on Nov 3.
In the earlier suit, the High Court set Oct 16 to continue hearing the compensation assessment following the government's settlement offer.
The dispute began in 2003 when Semantan Estate sued the government, alleging that the land had been acquired illegally. In 2009, the High Court ruled in the company's favour, finding that the acquisition was illegal and that Semantan Estate had a beneficial interest in the land.
The government's subsequent appeals were unsuccessful. In February 2017, Semantan Estate filed a suit to enforce the 2009 judgment.
A High Court order in August 2024 directing the transfer of the land title was later overturned by the Court of Appeal, leading to the current compensation assessment proceedings.
On Nov 13, 2025, the Federal Court dismissed Semantan Estate's application for leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal's decision that the Federal Territories Land Titles Registrar was not required to register 263.272 acres (106.54 hectares) of land in Duta Enclave in the company's name.
The Court of Appeal's decision in favour of the government remains in force because Semantan Estate failed to obtain leave to appeal to the Federal Court. The case was then returned to the High Court for an assessment of damages.
On June 24, 2025, the Court of Appeal ruled that Semantan Estate was not entitled to the land title but was entitled to appropriate compensation, to be assessed based on the land's value in 1956, when the government acquired it.
The disputed land is in the prime Jalan Duta area, known as the Duta Enclave, which houses government buildings including the National Hockey Stadium, the Malaysian Integrity Institute, the National Archives, the Kuala Lumpur Syariah Court, the Inland Revenue Board and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Academy. – BERNAMA

Title: Construction worker jailed three years for abducting, confining Palestinian man
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A construction worker was sentenced to three years' imprisonment by the High Court here today for abducting and confining a Palestinian man at a chalet four years ago.
Judge Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin imposed the sentence on Edy Ko'im Said, 46, after he pleaded guilty to an alternative charge.
The court ordered the father of three to begin serving his sentence today.
According to the charge, Edy Ko'im forcibly abducted the 31-year-old victim with the intention of secretly and unlawfully confining him at Jalan Mayang, Dang Wangi, here, at 10.40pm on Sept 28, 2022.
He was charged under Section 365 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum seven-year jail term and a fine.
According to the case facts, the victim was abducted and held at a chalet in Hulu Langat, Selangor, before police rescued him during a raid based on intelligence. He was found with his hands and feet bound with cable ties.
"Given the seriousness of the offence, the prosecution urges the court to impose an appropriate prison term on the accused," Deputy Public Prosecutor Mahadhir Mohd Khairudin said.
Defence counsel Kelvinder Singh Sidhu urged the court to impose the minimum prison term, citing his client's responsibility to support his wife and three children.
Meanwhile, the trial of seven other accused charged with kidnapping the same victim continued today.
They are Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 45, Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 45, Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 46, Muhammad Iqmal Abdul Rahis, 31, Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 60, Nidarahayu Zainal, 40, and Raibafie Amdan, 45.
According to the charge, all the accused had acted with a common intention to detain the victim at the same location and time to obtain a reward in exchange for secret information on developing and deactivating computer software used to hack mobile phones.
The eight accused were charged under Section 3 of the Kidnapping Act 1961, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code. If convicted, they face a prison term of between 30 and 40 years and whipping.
Apart from the kidnapping case, Tengku Arif Bongsu, Nidarahayu and her husband, Raibafie, face 19 money laundering charges involving more than RM250,000 under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLATFPUAA).
On July 10, 2025, six men were sentenced to five years' imprisonment after pleading guilty to alternative charges of abducting and confining the same victim.
They were Mohamad Norakmal Hassan, 46, Mohd Azwan Jamaludin, 42, Dody Junaidi, 47, Mohamad Sufian Saly, 28, Tengku Hazarul Ismail Tengku Hamid, 54, and Muhammad Al Hatim Mohd Fauzi, 28.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Retaining wall collapses after heavy rain, damaging six vehicles in Kajang [WATCH]
Article:
KAJANG: A five-metre-high retaining wall is believed to have given way following heavy rain, triggering a landslip that damaged six vehicles parked along Jalan Nilam here this evening.
The incident, which occurred around 5pm, damaged three cars and three motorcycles when soil came crashing down onto the vehicles.
Kajang police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said preliminary investigations indicated that the retaining wall had failed to withstand soil movement following heavy rain that began around 3pm.
"Initial investigations found that the incident is believed to have occurred when a retaining wall, estimated to be five metres high, failed to withstand soil movement following heavy rain in the area.
"The collapse caused soil to fall onto several vehicles parked near the affected area," he said in a statement.
Naazron said the three cars damaged in the incident were a Proton Saga, Proton Satria and Proton Wira Aeroback.
"Three motorcycles, comprising a Yamaha Nouvo, Honda Wave and Yamaha Lagenda, were also damaged.
"No casualties or injuries were reported," he said.
He added that the exact cause of the landslide is still being examined and remains under further investigation by the relevant authorities.
Meanwhile, security company operations officer Wan Nabihah Ramly, 35, who was at a premises near the landslip site, said she was still on duty when the incident occurred.
Wan Nabihah, who has worked in the area for two years, said this was the first time she had witnessed such an incident there.
"We were still working when we suddenly heard what sounded like something falling around 4.50pm.
"Around 5pm, there was a loud noise and people began shouting for everyone to get out.
"When we looked outside, everything had already collapsed. It all happened so quickly," she said when met at the scene.
Wan Nabihah said she believed the rainfall had contributed to the collapse after observing water flowing down the slope and carrying soil with it.
She said the fencing along the affected area had only been installed several months earlier, giving those working nearby a sense of security.
"The fence was only put up a few months ago, so those of us working here thought the area was secure.
"But when this happened, we realised that might not have been the case," she said.
She believed the prolonged rainfall could have weakened the soil, although the actual cause of the collapse has yet to be determined by the authorities.
Wan Nabihah said the incident was particularly unsettling as nothing similar had occurred during her two years working in the area.
It was reported that three cars
and three motorcycles were buried in a landslip along Jalan Nilam 2, here. this evening.
However, no casualties were reported, and authorities confirmed that no one was trapped inside the affected vehicles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Federal-state cooperation key to sustainable development, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Close cooperation between the federal and state governments is key to ensuring inclusive and sustainable national development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said this while chairing the 51st National Physical Planning Council (MPFN) meeting in Putrajaya today.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the meeting reviewed various aspects of national physical development, including land-use planning and state structure plans, in accordance with the Town and Country Planning Act .
"All relevant parties must continue to improve service delivery to strengthen the investment ecosystem and make dealings easier for the people," he said.
Meanwhile, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said the meeting had agreed that comprehensive geological mapping be carried out along roads and in other areas to detect potential sinkhole threats.
He said the geological mapping exercise should be conducted in collaboration with local authorities.
"Various matters were discussed at this afternoon's MPFN meeting, and the issue or threat of sinkholes was of particular concern to me.
"Serious attention must be given, especially to risk assessment and the ability to detect sinkhole threats, as these involve lives, safety and potential losses," he said in a Facebook post.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Boy, 7, injured in stray dog attack in Lima Kedai
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: A 7-year-old boy was injured after being attacked by a pack of six to eight stray dogs while playing at a playground near a low-cost flat in Lima Kedai here today.
Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad said the incident occurred between 3pm and 4pm, when the boy was playing in the area before the dogs attacked him, causing him to fall and roll on the ground as he tried to escape.
"Fortunately, a man who witnessed the incident threw stones at the dogs from a distance to save the boy.
"I was informed of the incident by the village head and went to the flats to inspect the location," he told Bernama when contacted.
He said the victim sustained injuries to the eye area, neck, head and body and was rushed to Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) in Johor Baru for treatment.
Pandak said such incidents are deeply concerning and require immediate action by authorities.
He said the incident was not the first of its kind in the area, as a 15-year-old boy had also been attacked by a pack of eight stray dogs around 6am the same day.
The teenager managed to drive the dogs away before fleeing to the building's staircase, but sustained injuries to his leg.
Pandak said he had met the teenager and advised him to seek treatment at a nearby clinic.
He said the Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) would conduct an operation tonight to address the stray dog problem in the area.
He said appropriate action needs to be taken immediately to ensure the safety of the residents even if it might draw objections from non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
"How long are we going to allow this to happen? Do we have to wait for someone to die before action is taken?" he said.
In an earlier incident on Sept 5, a two-year-old girl, Nur Haira Wafiqah, was reported to have sustained serious injuries after being attacked by five stray dogs in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, Batu Pahat.
The victim suffered serious injuries to several parts of her body in the attack.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Firefly cancels Subang-Singapore flights until October 14 as haze persists
Article:
SINGAPORE, Oct 12 — Prevailing weather and haze conditions have forced Firefly to extend flight cancellations between Subang and Singapore’s Seletar Airport until October 14, with affected passengers being offered alternative Malaysia Airlines flights, subject to seat availability, or full refunds.
Firefly, a wholly owned subsidiary of Malaysia Airlines, had earlier cancelled all scheduled flights between Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang and Seletar Airport from October 10 to 12 as a precautionary safety measure.
In an advisory on Monday, the airline said the extended cancellations involved six daily services: FY3122 and FY3123, FY3124 and FY3125, FY3126 and FY3127, FY3128 and FY3129, FY3130 and FY3131, as well as FY3132 and FY3133.
“Affected passengers are being contacted and reallocated onto available Malaysia Airlines services via the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore route, subject to seat availability.
“Passengers who opt not to proceed with the reallocated flights are eligible for a full refund, which will be credited back to the original payment method within 30 working days,” it said.
Meanwhile, Singapore’s air quality remained unhealthy on Monday, with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) ranging from 118 to 155 as of 7 pm, according to the National Environment Agency (NEA).
Readings stood at 155 in the central and west regions, 139 in the east, 122 in the south and 118 in the north. — Bernama

Title: Federal-state cooperation key to inclusive, sustainable development, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Close cooperation between the federal and state governments is essential to ensuring that national development is planned in an inclusive, sustainable and comprehensive manner for the benefit of the people.
In a Facebook post, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he made the remarks while chairing the 51st National Physical Planning Council (MPFN) meeting in Putrajaya today.
