Title: Kedah police: Motorcycle theft allegation believed to have led to teen’s torture death
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 12 — An allegation that an 18-year-old youth had stolen a motorcycle is believed to have prompted a group of suspects to torture him before his body was found by the roadside in Jalan Harvard, Gurun, last Thursday.
Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said police received information about the discovery of the body at 8.05am on October 8, while a post-mortem found that the victim had died from blunt force trauma to the head.
He said the suspects were believed to have acted out of anger after receiving complaints from local residents that the victim had stolen a motorcycle.
“The victim was caught in Pendang on October 5 before being taken to the house of one of the suspects, where he was detained for two days, tortured and beaten, and had his hair cut,” he told reporters at the Kedah Contingent Police Headquarters here today.
Adzli said the victim was found dead inside the house on the night of October 7, and his body was subsequently dumped by the roadside.
He said police arrested 14 men aged between 16 and 24 in operations around Gurun and Guar Chempedak from noon to 8.30pm on October 8, a few hours after the body was discovered.
Police seized 14 mobile phones, a Honda City, scissors and the victim’s identity card. Twelve suspects have been remanded for six days until Wednesday, while two underage suspects have been remanded until tomorrow. The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
The victim, identified as Muhammad Haikal Mohd Shahrilnizam, 18, was found wearing yellow and black sportswear and had injuries to his head and face. He was initially found without identification documents.
In a separate case, Adzli said police were tracking down two men to assist in investigations into an attempted murder and obstructing police officers from carrying out their duties during Ops Pintas, an operation against migrant smuggling at the Hutan Kampung Toll Plaza here on October 7.
He said police had intercepted a Proton X70 SUV suspected of carrying five migrants, but the driver allegedly acted aggressively, attempted to run over a police officer and crashed into the toll barrier.
“Police fired one shot at the tyre, but the suspect fled and abandoned the vehicle in Pendang, about 28.3 kilometres from the scene,” he said.
Adzli said several individuals had been detained, while police were seeking Muhammad Raffi Yusrino, 28, and Zulfikrie Naaim Morhinino, 36, to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Finance Ministry to strengthen oversight of public funds through amended Audit Act, new procurement law
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Finance Ministry will use amendments to the Audit Act 1957 and the Government Procurement Act 2026 to strengthen oversight of public funds and improve transparency in government spending.
Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said the amended Audit Act gives the Auditor-General greater scope to trace funds across government agencies and examine how the money is used.
“The government has also approved the Government Procurement Act, which enables the government to tighten oversight in terms of transparency and value for money in the procurement process.
“The Act will be enforced next year, where the government will also share details on companies receiving the contracts,” Johan said.
The Government Procurement Act 2026 was gazetted on May 26 and is expected to come into operation in 2027, subject to a commencement date appointed by the Finance Minister through a gazette notification.
Johan said governance would be further strengthened through a proposed Government-Owned Entities Bill, which is intended to improve oversight of procurement and investment by government-owned entities, including government-linked companies and statutory bodies.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had previously said the proposed Bill was intended to prevent major financial scandals, including 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), and mismanagement involving Tabung Haji and Felda, from recurring.
Separately, Anwar said the Government Procurement Act would improve transparency through the publication of project details, including the names of contractors and contract values, once it comes into force in 2027.
“When governance is corrected, the benefits resulting from the change will contribute to the people’s welfare,” Anwar said previously.

Title: Malaysia targets 3.3pc fiscal deficit in 2027, 3pc by 2028, says Treasury sec-gen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Malaysia is targeting a fiscal deficit of 3.3 per cent next year as it presses ahead with plans to bring the figure down to 3 per cent by 2028, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said today.
Speaking at a panel discussion titled “Post-Budget 2027 Debate” organised by the Malaysian Economic Association in Kuala Lumpur, Johan said fiscal consolidation remained a key government priority, particularly in maintaining investor confidence.
“This is an area where the government is placing strong emphasis on.
“This is so Malaysia can demonstrate our ability to execute disciplined and prudent financial management.
“As such we remain committed to the pledges made under the Fiscal Responsibility Act — so that we can achieve a fiscal deficit as low as three per cent by 2028,” he said.
The government is targeting a fiscal deficit of 3.6 per cent this year, after reducing it from 5.5 per cent in 2022 to 3.7 per cent in 2025.
Johan said uncertainty in the Middle East and the possibility of higher oil prices had been factored into the government's planning for next year.
“Consequently, we estimate that this year’s subsidy allocation of around RM40 billion will be maintained into next year.
“However, just as was practiced this year when oil prices rose higher than anticipated, we will make adjustments according to circumstances,” he said.
The government's fiscal consolidation efforts are guided by the Public Finance and Fiscal Responsibility Act 2023, which provides a framework for responsible management of public finances.

Title: Seven-year-old seriously injured in Johor stray dog attack, teen escapes unhurt in earlier incident at same location
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 12 — A seven-year-old boy suffered serious injuries after he was attacked by eight stray dogs while playing at a playground at a housing complex in Lima Kedai here today.
During the incident, which occurred at 3pm, the primary one pupil suffered injuries to his eyes, neck, head, and body before being rushed to Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) in Johor Bahru for treatment.
Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad expressed concern over the incident urging authorities to address the issue of stray dogs.
“Immediate measures are required to prevent a recurrence of such incidents, particularly those involving children and residents using public facilities within the housing complex,” he said after visiting the victim at his home here today.
Pandak said the incident involving the child was the second to occur today.
He said he was informed that an earlier incident took place at 6am, where an 18-year-old male was attacked by a pack of stray dogs at the same location.
“However, the teenager managed to fend off the animals without sustaining any injuries, he said, adding that the incidents, occurring within a span of just a few hours, have raised concerns regarding the safety of residents, especially children.
Pandak hopes the relevant authorities will take immediate action to ensure the safety of residents in Lima Kedai.
He said an effective plan is needed to resolve the issue of stray dogs.

Title: Govt aims to improve water quality in 33 polluted rivers in Malaysia by 10pc, says DPM Fadillah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The government aims to improve the Water Quality Index (WQI) of 33 rivers identified as polluted in 2025 by at least 10 per cent within a year, with appropriate recognition to be given to state governments that achieve the target.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said the target was set at the second 2026 meeting of the National Special Committee on Addressing River Water Quality Deterioration, which he chaired today.
Fadillah, who is also Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister, said Department of Environment (DOE) reports showed that the number of polluted rivers rose from 25 in 2023 to 27 in 2024 and 33 in 2025.
In Selangor, the Selangor Water Management Authority (Luas) reported 144 cases of water source pollution detected over the three years up to September 14, 2026, with varying levels of risk.
“I appreciate the commitment of Luas and relevant agencies nationwide in detecting and addressing pollution. However, this increase clearly shows that existing measures need to be strengthened through more effective, coordinated and sustained action,” he said in a Facebook post.
Fadillah said polluted rivers could disrupt water treatment plant operations, affect public water supplies, increase treatment costs and affect economic activities, underscoring the need to make water resource protection a shared priority at all levels of administration.
He said the meeting also decided to conduct a pilot study on the integrated management of non-point source (NPS) pollution at a selected local authority area to test the applicability of field data, estimate pollution loads, identify priority areas and formulate appropriate control measures.
In addition, a Technical Committee on Effluent Discharge Standards, chaired by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government, will be established in collaboration with the National Water Research Institute of Malaysia (NAHRIM) to coordinate the implementation of effluent discharge standards in urban and rural areas.
The meeting also saw the launch of the Guidelines for the Installation of Floating Solar Panels on Water Reservoirs and Lakes in Malaysia, which will serve as a reference to ensure that floating solar developments are carried out in a planned and sustainable manner while safeguarding the country’s water resources.
The integrated efforts reflected the government’s commitment to tackling pollution at its source, protecting water resources and safeguarding national water security through cooperation between the federal government, state governments, local authorities and all stakeholders, he added. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Pet vaccination, sterilisation eligible for tax relief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The government proposes expanding the scope of individual income tax relief for lifestyle to include pet care expenses, such as vaccinations and sterilisation treatments by registered veterinary services.
In the Budget 2027 tax measures document, the Ministry of Finance (MoF) said the expansion would also cover the costs of adopting a rescued pet from a registered animal shelter.
The proposal aims to cultivate kindness and empathy toward animals in need of care.
MoF said the personal income tax relief cap for lifestyle remains at RM2,500, including the proposed expansion.
Additionally, to promote digital literacy and the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technology to boost productivity and drive innovation, the scope of the personal income tax relief for lifestyle is proposed to be expanded to include subscription costs for AI software and applications for personal use, spouses, or children.
Currently, beginning with the 2024 assessment year, the personal income tax relief for lifestyle is limited to RM2,500 and covers the purchase of reading materials, including e-books and daily newspapers in print/electronic form, as well as personal computers, smartphones, or tablets, and internet subscriptions. — Bernama

Title: High Court allows MCMC’s preliminary objection, Papagomo committal hearing on Dec 23
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The High Court will first hear the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s (MCMC) committal application against blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, also known as Papagomo, before proceeding with the inter-partes injunction hearing.
MCMC’s counsel, Datuk Selva Mookiah, when confirming the matter said Judge Datuk Dr Arik Sanusi Yeop Johari made the ruling after allowing MCMC’s preliminary objection that the committal application should be heard first, as Wan Azri must purge the contempt first, before proceeding with the inter-partes injunction hearing.
He said the court fixed December 23 to hear both matters.
“The court also extended the existing ad interim injunction against Wan Muhammad Azri until December 23. The committal hearing will determine the allegation of contempt of court, while the inter partes hearing will consider the injunction in the presence of both parties,” he said.
On June 19, the court granted an ex parte interim injunction sought by the MCMC, restraining Wan Muhammad Azri from publishing allegedly defamatory statements against the commission and ordering him to immediately cease publishing and disseminating harmful online content through social media.
The order also prohibits Wan Muhammad Azri from using any social media platform, whether through existing or new accounts, to publish or distribute false, misleading or harmful content.
On August 6, Wan Azri used Facebook and/or YouTube social media platforms to publish and/or cause to be published a live session containing false, misleading and/or harmful online contents, in breach of the ad interim injunction dated July 6.
Therefore, MCMC has applied to the court for leave to commence a committal proceeding against Wan Azri.
On October 6, the court granted MCMC leave to initiate committal proceedings against Wan Muhammad Azri over an alleged breach of the injunction through a live session published on Facebook and/or YouTube on August 6.
On May 27, the MCMC filed the suit, alleging that Wan Muhammad Azri had posted defamatory statements on social media claiming the commission had censored court reports relating to Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil’s case against him.
In its statement of claim, the MCMC said it had never been involved in any form of censorship regarding reports on the Kuala Lumpur High Court proceedings involving Fahmi and the defendant.
The commission maintained that the defendant’s allegations were false, baseless and had undermined public confidence in the regulator. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Jordan seek high-tech cooperation to train more engineers, says Anwar
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 12 — Malaysia and Jordan are seeking to expand strategic cooperation in high-tech industries, particularly semiconductors and advanced technical education and training, to develop more engineers and skilled workers for future industry needs.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said these were among the key areas discussed during his meeting today with Jordan’s King Abdullah II, who was on a two-day state visit to the country at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
He said the talks focused on strengthening bilateral ties in higher education, skilled human capital development, emerging technologies and the semiconductor ecosystem.
“We also discussed potential cooperation in developing advanced technical education and training centres, including producing more engineers and skilled workers to meet future industry demands,” he posted on Facebook.
Anwar said discussions also covered expanding trade and investment, including a potential free trade agreement (FTA), tariff restructuring, stronger supply chains and cooperation in energy, transport, the halal industry and tourism.
Anwar said he and King Abdullah also exchanged views on geopolitical developments in West Asia, particularly in Palestine and Syria, and their implications for regional security and stability.
He said they also agreed on the urgent need to end atrocities against Palestinians, including continued violence and rights violations in Jerusalem and the West Bank.
“I stressed that Malaysia will remain steadfast in championing Palestinian rights while strengthening humanitarian assistance, particularly for the people of Gaza,” he said.
Anwar noted that the Jordanian monarch also expressed appreciation for Malaysia’s stance and efforts in supporting the Palestinian cause.
Anwar also expressed hope that the meeting would elevate Malaysia-Jordan relations through closer economic and technological cooperation, as well as shared commitments to humanity, peace and global justice.
The state visit was King Abdullah’s second to Malaysia since May 2008, as both countries marked more than six decades of diplomatic relations established in 1965.
Prior to his departure after concluding the visit, King Abdullah granted Anwar an audience at the Bunga Raya Complex, Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), for about 30 minutes to discuss strengthening longstanding bilateral relations.
Bilateral trade reached RM993.4 million in 2025, up 15.2 per cent from 2024, while trade from January to August 2026 rose eight per cent year-on-year to RM740.7 million. — Bernama

Title: TNB confirms electrical accident at its installation in Johor’s Kota Tinggi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) has confirmed an electrical accident involving a member of the public at one of its installations in Kota Tinggi, Johor, today.
In a statement posted on Facebook by TNB CareLine, the utility company said its technical team was dispatched to the location shortly after receiving a report of the incident.
TNB said the incident was believed to be linked to vandalism and that it would provide full support and cooperation to the authorities in their further investigations.
The company also advised the public against tampering with, opening or approaching electrical installations, warning that such actions could result in serious injury or death.

Title: No need to replace old birth certificates, still valid, says NRD; new copies cost RM5
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 12 — Old birth certificates, including handwritten documents issued in paper format, remain valid and do not need to be replaced, said National Registration Department (NRD) director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias.
He said those who wished to obtain a birth certificate in the new format could apply for an extract at any NRD office for RM5, with the process taking less than five minutes.
“Birth certificates are never invalid, whether they are from the older or newer generation,” he told reporters after the Registration Literacy Programme held in conjunction with the Kelantan-level 78th National Registration Day celebration at Pos Balar here today.
Badrul Hisham said birth documentation was essential to establish a legally recognised identity and ensure individuals could access their rights and services as Malaysians.
He said the NRD continued to reach out to communities, including the Orang Asli in rural areas, to ensure they had access to registration and documentation services.
Asked about the number of Orang Asli who had yet to obtain a MyKad or birth certificate, he said the department did not have exact figures, as it could only identify those who came forward to seek its services.
He said awareness efforts on the importance of personal documentation needed to continue through outreach programmes and cooperation with relevant agencies to ensure no one was left out of the national registration system. — Bernama

Title: Kedah police bust online scam syndicate posing as Indian police officers
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 12 — Kedah police successfully crippled an online scam syndicate involving suspects posing as Indian police officers during a raid on a business premises in Bandar Putra, Kulim, last Friday.
Kedah Police Chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said that during the joint operation at 8pm, police arrested 48 individuals suspected of acting as syndicate members, comprising seven locals, eight Indian nationals, and 33 Pakistani nationals.
“This syndicate began operating late last August at a three-story shoplot running online scam activities by impersonating as police officers from India, targeting victims from that country.
“They used the Telegram app to communicate and deceive victims by claiming the victims’ phone numbers were involved in illegal activities. Victims were asked to transfer money into provided bank accounts for police investigation purposes,” he told reporters at the Kedah Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) here today.
He added that investigations into the syndicate members, aged 20 to 43, revealed that they claimed they were duped after applying for jobs offered on social media before being added to a Telegram group and promised salaries of around RM2,500 to RM3,500 a month.
“Investigations also found that the syndicate members failed to present valid travel documents for entry into Malaysia. So far, a total of 73 individuals have fallen victim to this syndicate’s scams, involving losses of nearly RM1.4 million.
“Additionally, police seized various items including 89 mobile phones, seven laptops, modems, monitors, Indian police uniforms, Indian flags, Indian Central Bureau of Investigation flags, and several other items. The total value of the seizures is estimated at RM70,000,” he said.
Adzli further added that the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code (PC), Section 120B of the PC, and Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Meanwhile, he noted that follow-up arrests were made at 6:00 pm yesterday involving two local men and three local women aged 44 to 51, who acted as the premises owners, real estate agents, and renters of the involved premises.
“All these arrests were made around Kulim and Tanjung Piandang, Perak, and checks revealed that the five new suspects arrested have no prior criminal records.
“The success of this operation is the result of public information, so the police would like to thank the public for staying alert to their surroundings. If there is any information regarding scam activities, please channel the information to enable prompt action to be taken,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Two killed, two injured in three-vehicle pile-up on Federal Highway
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Two men were killed while two others were injured in an accident involving three cars at Kilometer 18.2 of the Federal Highway heading towards Kuala Lumpur, early this morning.
Petaling Jaya District Police Chief ACP Shamsudin Mamat said the accident, which occurred at approximately 12.20am, involved a Proton Wira driven by a local man in his 20s who was travelling from Shah Alam to Kuala Lumpur.
He said that preliminary investigations found the driver of the Proton Wira was believed to have failed to control his vehicle before crashing into the road divider on the right side of the highway, triggering a collision with two other cars traveling behind it.
“As a result of the accident, the driver of the Proton Wira and a passenger in his 20s suffered severe injuries and were confirmed dead at the scene.
“Two other passengers, who were friends of the victims, sustained injuries to their bodies,” he said in a statement today.
Shamsudin said the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters received a report regarding the fatal accident at 1:05 am today.
He stated that the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
In the meantime, he reminded all road users to always comply with traffic laws to prevent accidents.
“The police will not compromise with road users who do not obey regulations and will take firm action against any road user who violates the law,” he said.
Shamsudin also appealed to witnesses who saw or were at the scene to come forward to the nearest police station or contact the traffic investigating officer, Insp Mohd Nazar Md Kasim, at 012-5653395 to assist with the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Opposition leader criticises GLC involvement in non-core projects in Budget 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today alleged that government-linked corporations (GLCs) were being made to operate beyond their core mandates.
While debating Budget 2027, he cited a project to build a hostel for students that he said would be funded by the Retirement Fund Incorporated (KWAP), alleging this practice extended to others such as Petronas, Tenaga Nasional Bhd, and more.
"Too many of them have been used...for example, KWAP's fundamental purpose is to preserve and grow that capital so it can cover future pensions for retirees or those eligible to receive them,” he said during today’s debate.
"So why is the government asking KWAP to go and build student hostels? Where are the financial returns? I am truly bewildered at times."
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled a record RM459 billion federal spending plan for 2027 last Friday, in which he also outlined a RM50 billion from government-linked investment companies, state enterprises and statutory bodies.
Hamzah criticised this today, saying the GLCs should not be involved with industries beyond their own to prevent a loss of focus.

Title: 1MDB in talks to settle lawsuit with Deutsche Bank
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 12 — 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) is in talks with Deutsche Bank (Malaysia) Berhad to settle a lawsuit filed against the bank.
1MDB’s counsel, Datuk Lim Chee Wee, informed the Federal Court of the settlement talks during proceedings today before a three-member panel led by Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah.
The panel, comprising Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Seri Azizah Nawawi and Federal Court Judge Datuk Ravinthran N. Paramaguru, was hearing 1MDB’s application for leave to appeal against a decision in favour of UK law firm White & Case LLP.
“We have already informed the High Court that there is a proposed settlement between our client (1MDB) and Deutsche Bank. The hearing for that case is scheduled for October 26 before High Court Judicial Commissioner Rihada Rafie,” Lim said.
However, the terms of the proposed settlement were not disclosed.
On May 7, 2021, 1MDB filed a US$1.83 billion suit against seven defendants, alleging breach of contract, negligence and criminal conspiracy in the misappropriation of its funds.
1MDB named Deutsche Bank (Malaysia) Berhad, Coutts & Co, JP Morgan (Switzerland), Petrosaudi International, Petrosaudi Holdings (Cayman), Tarik Obaid and Patrick Mahony as the first to seventh defendants.
The plaintiff alleged that all the defendants conspired to defraud 1MDB, and provided dishonest assistance causing losses to the company as well as damaging 1MDB’s reputation and good name.
However, on November 13, last year, 1MDB had dropped JPMorgan and Coutts and Co from the suit.
Meanwhile, on 1MDB’s application for leave to appeal to the Federal Court, counsel Datuk Dr Cyrus Das, representing White & Case, told the panel that he objected to 1MDB’s application to include more than 3,000 pages of additional documents in support of its leave application.
Another counsel for 1MDB, Khoo Guan Huat, informed the court that the issue had been raised during case management before the Federal Court last week.
The panel then allowed 1MDB’s application to include the additional documents and directed that affidavits be filed. The court also ordered that case management be held today to fix an early hearing date for the application.
On August 20, this year, the Court of Appeal granted an appeal by White & Case LLP against a High Court decision that allowed a lawsuit filed by 1MDB on alleged fraud to be heard in Malaysia, ruling that the High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear 1MDB’s suit against the firm.
1MDB filed the suit in the Kuala Lumpur High Court in 2024, seeking US$1.83 billion and US$33 million in losses from White & Case and Mahony. The fund alleged that White & Case assisted PetroSaudi in committing fraud and conspired to harm 1MDB while acting as its legal counsel.
Last year, the High Court rejected White & Case’s challenge, ruling that it could hear the lawsuit because the trial witnesses are located in Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan ruler to skip Conference of Rulers meeting, palace says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, will not attend the Conference of Rulers meeting scheduled from October 13 to 15, the Negeri Sembilan Palace said today.
In a statement, Royal Comptroller Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali said attendance at the Conference of Rulers meeting did not require an invitation.
He also clarified that Tuanku Muhriz had not received any letter or formal invitation from the meeting’s chairman, Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah, to attend the pre-council meeting.
Azizi said Tuanku Muhriz had decided not to attend the meeting and would instead focus on state affairs, particularly the ceremony for the appointment of the new Undang of Jelebu.
The palace also stressed that it had not previously issued any media statement on the matter to any party or media organisation.

Title: High Court jails construction worker three years for Palestinian abduction tied to hacking secrets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — A construction worker who was previously charged with kidnapping a Palestinian man was sentenced to three years in prison by the High Court here today for abducting and confining the man at a chalet four years ago.
Judge Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin imposed the sentence on Edy Ko’im Said, 46, after he pleaded guilty to an alternative charge of abducting and confining the Palestinian man.
The court ordered the father of three to begin serving his prison sentence today.
According to the alternative charge, Edy Ko’im was accused of forcibly abducting the 31-year-old victim with the intention of secretly and unlawfully confining him at Jalan Mayang, Dang Wangi, here, at 10.40 pm on Sept 28, 2022.
He was charged under Section 365 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum prison sentence of seven years and also provides for a fine.
According to the case facts, the Palestinian man was abducted and held at a chalet in Hulu Langat, Selangor, before police rescued him in a raid based on intelligence. The victim was found with his hands and feet bound with cable ties.
“Given the seriousness of the offence, the prosecution urges the court to impose an appropriate prison term on the accused,” Deputy Public Prosecutor Mahadhir Mohd Khairudin said.
Defence counsel Kelvinder Singh Sidhu urged the court to impose the minimum prison term, citing his client’s responsibility to support his wife and three children.
Meanwhile, the trial of seven other accused charged with kidnapping the same victim continued today. They are Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 45, Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 45, Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 46, Muhammad Iqmal Abdul Rahis, 31, Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 60, Nidarahayu Zainal, 40, and Raibafie Amdan, 45.
According to the charge, all the accused had acted with a common intention to detain the victim at the same location and time to obtain a reward in exchange for secret information on developing and deactivating computer software used to hack mobile phones.
The eight accused were charged under Section 3 of the Kidnapping Act 1961, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code. If convicted, they face a prison term of between 30 and 40 years and whipping.
Apart from the kidnapping case, Tengku Arif Bongsu, Nidarahayu and her husband, Raibafie, face 19 money laundering charges involving more than RM250,000 under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLATFPUAA).
On July 10, 2025, six men were sentenced to five years’ imprisonment after pleading guilty to alternative charges of abducting and confining the same victim. They were Mohamad Norakmal Hassan, 46, Mohd Azwan Jamaludin, 42, Dody Junaidi, 47, Mohamad Sufian Saly, 28, Tengku Hazarul Ismail Tengku Hamid, 54, and Muhammad Al Hatim Mohd Fauzi, 28. — Bernama

Title: Batik Air: Flight OD701 from KLIA to Jeddah called off as precautionary measure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Batik Air has cancelled its scheduled flight from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, today as a precautionary measure amid the ongoing conflict.
In a statement today, the airline said the decision was made following an assessment of the evolving situation, with the safety and security of passengers and crew remaining its highest priority.
“The affected flight, OD701, was scheduled to depart Kuala Lumpur for King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah at 7.25pm.
“Affected passengers have been rescheduled to the next available flight and will be notified through their registered contact details, where applicable,” it said.
The airline said it was closely monitoring developments and coordinating with the relevant aviation authorities, airport operators and other stakeholders to assess the potential impact on flight operations.
Passengers were also advised to check Batik Air’s official website and social media channels for the latest flight updates.
Earlier today, Bernama reported that Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan had advised Malaysians to temporarily postpone travel to Saudi Arabia for umrah following security concerns after a deadly attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. — Bernama

Title: Haze worsens: 23 stations record ‘Unhealthy’ API levels across Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Air quality worsened across the country this afternoon, with 23 of the nation's 68 monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, according to the Department of Environment (DOE).
As of 4.50pm, 41 stations recorded moderate air quality and four were in the good range. No station recorded very unhealthy or hazardous levels. An Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 101 to 200 is classed as unhealthy.
Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded the highest reading at 174, followed by Kota Tinggi, also in Johor, at 170. Seremban in Negeri Sembilan was third at 167, followed by Pengerang in Johor at 166 and Nilai in Negeri Sembilan at 164.
Johor had seven stations in the unhealthy range. Besides Pasir Gudang, Kota Tinggi and Pengerang, the others were Larkin at 160, Batu Pahat at 156, Tangkak at 152 and Kluang at 151. Segamat, which was in the unhealthy range this morning, no longer appeared on the list.
Negeri Sembilan had three unhealthy stations, with Port Dickson at 154 in addition to Seremban and Nilai.
In Melaka, Bukit Rambai logged 161, Bandaraya Melaka 155 and Alor Gajah 153. Putrajaya recorded 156, up from 146 this morning and above the 150 mark that authorities there had cited as the closure threshold.
In Pahang, Balok Baru in Kuantan recorded 162 and Rompin 155. In Terengganu, Kemaman recorded 155 and Paka 153, while Johan Setia in Selangor stood at 152.
Unhealthy readings also appeared in East Malaysia, which was not among the areas listed this morning. In Sarawak, IPD Serian recorded 155, Sri Aman 153 and Samarahan 148, while in Sabah, Tawau logged 149.
Several readings have also risen since the morning. Pasir Gudang climbed from 168 to 174, Seremban from 164 to 167, and Bukit Rambai from 153 to 161. Alor Gajah in Melaka jumped from 101 to 153, Port Dickson from 137 to 154 and Johan Setia from 129 to 152. Kota Tinggi held at 170.
Earlier, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek announced that schools in Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan and Putrajaya will be closed tomorrow.
The closures also cover schools under the district education offices of Hulu Langat, Petaling Perdana, Kuala Langat and Sepang in Selangor, and Kuantan and Rompin in Pahang. Schools elsewhere will operate as usual.
Health and education authorities have advised parents, high-risk groups and students with respiratory symptoms to wear face masks and check real-time air quality updates through official channels.

Title: Fadhlina: Schools closed tomorrow in Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Putrajaya as haze worsens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Schools across Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, and Putrajaya, as well as several districts in Selangor and Pahang, will be closed tomorrow following a sharp deterioration in air quality, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek announced today.
In a statement posted on her official Facebook page, Fadhlina confirmed that all primary and secondary schools in the three states and the federal administrative centre will suspend physical classes tomorrow.
The mandatory closures also extend to schools under four District Education Offices (PPD) in Selangor: Hulu Langat, Petaling Perdana, Kuala Langat, and Sepang. In Pahang, schools under PPD Kuantan and PPD Rompin will likewise remain closed.
Schools in all other unaffected states and districts will operate as normal, the minister said.
The nationwide shutdown follows a sudden rebound in transboundary smoke pollution, with Department of Environment (DOE) data recording 22 out of 68 national monitoring stations in the unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) bracket (101 to 200) earlier today.
Johor was the hardest hit nationwide, logging eight unhealthy stations led by the country's peak reading of 170 in Kota Tinggi. In Negeri Sembilan, Seremban registered 164 and Nilai recorded 163. In Pahang, Balok Baru in Kuantan posted 162 and Rompin stood at 157, while Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded 153. Putrajaya logged 146, nearing the 150 closure threshold.
Several affected districts had only resumed physical classroom sessions this morning after experiencing moderate air quality over the weekend.
Health and education authorities have urged parents, educators, and high-risk students with chronic respiratory conditions to wear protective face masks outdoors and closely track hourly API updates via official channels.

Title: Kuraman Island sand spit stretches into record books, spurring Labuan’s ecotourism appeal
Article:
LABUAN, Oct 12 — The natural sand spit on Kuraman Island has set two national records in the Malaysia Book of Records (MBR), with its total length measuring 808.4 metres and its exposed section measuring 790.4 metres.
The two records are ‘Longest Natural Sand Spit in Malaysia’ (Beting Pasir Semula Jadi Terpanjang di Malaysia) and ‘Longest Exposed Sand Spit in Malaysia’ (Beting Pasir Terdedah Terpanjang di Malaysia).
The certificate recognising the achievements was presented to Federal Territories Department director-general Datuk Muhammad Azmi Mohd Zain following the official declaration.
Muhammad Azmi said the recognition marked a significant milestone in efforts to promote Labuan’s geological heritage and tourism potential, while raising the profile of Kuraman Island and Labuan Geopark nationally.
Located west of Labuan near Rusukan Besar and Rusukan Kecil islands, Kuraman Island covers about 1.47 square kilometres (363 acres) and is the largest island in the Labuan Marine Park, which was gazetted in 1994.
The island’s main attraction is its natural sand spit, a distinctive geological formation extending into the sea.
Estimated to be about 35 million years old, it was formed through sediment deposition and the combined effects of longshore currents, waves and wind.
“The two MBR records were awarded based on measurements of the natural formation’s total length and exposed section. The recognition is expected to strengthen the island’s appeal as a geotourism destination, complementing its marine ecosystem, coastal scenery and distinctive geological landscape.
“It could also create opportunities for nature-based tourism and community-driven economic activities, including boat transport, recreational services, tour guiding, hospitality and small businesses,” he said to Bernama at the site today.
However, he said tourism development must be carried out responsibly to safeguard the island’s geological heritage and marine ecosystem.
“Kuraman Island is one of the key geosites under Labuan Geopark, offering visitors an opportunity to appreciate the relationship between geological history, marine biodiversity and coastal processes,” he said.
Muhammad Azmi said the recognition would support efforts to position Labuan as a tourism destination with a distinctive identity while ensuring the island’s natural heritage remains protected for future generations. — Daily Express

Title: Hannah Yeoh says DBKL, police mull joint control centre for KL’s 10,000 CCTVs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) are considering establishing a control centre to give the police better access to the closed-circuit television (CCTV) system across the federal capital.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the initiative is crucial as about 10,000 CCTV units are installed throughout Kuala Lumpur.
She added that it will enhance operational efficiency in monitoring and responding to security incidents and traffic flow.
“DBKL and the PDRM are indeed in discussions to establish a second command centre that is easily accessible to the Police.
“Currently, although DBKL has smart CCTVs, we rely heavily on the police to be on the ground to ensure smooth traffic flow,” she told reporters after handing over information and communications technology (ICT) equipment at the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD) here today.
Hannah, the Segambut MP, said RM60,000 has been allocated for ICT equipment for the front counters of Sentul IPD and three police stations under its administration.
She added that RM100,000 has also been allocated to cover part of the logistics costs for police personnel involved in programmes organised by DBKL.
Hannah said close cooperation between DBKL and the police is vital for managing events in the capital, including road closures for running events and concerts, as well as combating crime and online fraud.
Sentul police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the ICT system will significantly help speed up services to the public, especially when lodging police reports. — Bernama

Title: Education minister: Decisions on school haze closures guided by MetMalaysia, Health Ministry and NRES
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 12 — Decisions regarding the closure and reopening of schools due to the haze situation will be made periodically based on standard operating procedures (SOPs), existing guidelines, and advice from relevant agencies.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said these decisions depend on advice of the Malaysian Meteorological Department (METMalaysia) and the Ministry of Health (MOH), as well as the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES).
She noted that the Ministry of Education does not make such decisions in isolation, instead, it takes into account air quality assessments, health advice, and deliberations with relevant committees.
“We have established that we act based on SOPs, existing guidelines, and advice from MET in accordance with periodic directives as well as the Ministry of Health (MOH).
“We have a committee, and we fully adopt the guidelines provided by NRES and the MOH,” she told reporters after attending MOE’s ‘Petah KPM 2026’ programme here today.
Fadhlina said the current haze situation is being monitored according to established guidelines, however, parents must continue to prioritise their children’s health.
She advised parents not to send their children to school if they are unwell, but instead to inform the school of the situation.
“That is why, in the guidance we provide to parents, we state that if children are unwell, they should not be sent to school, and the school should be notified,” she said.
She also expressed appreciation for the cooperation of parents who pay attention to health issues and share their views with the Ministry of Education (MOE), helping the ministry make decisions regarding school management during the haze.
According to her, any decision must strike a balance between protecting students’ health and the impact on education should schools remain closed for an extended period.
Commenting on the possibility of the haze persisting until November or December, Fadhlina said decisions would continue to be made collaboratively, based on the guidelines and advice of relevant agencies.
‘Petah KPM’ serves as a strategic platform to holistically uphold the ‘Upholding the Malay Language and Strengthening the English Language’ (MBMMBI) policy as it emphasises that proficiency in both Malay and English must go hand-in-hand to foster a culture of fluent and courteous communication across diverse ethnic groups. — Bernama

Title: Opposition leader challenges Putrajaya to revive GST, end ‘uncertainty’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today alleged that the government’s hybrid taxation proposal was tacit admission that it was wrong to reject the goods and services tax (GST).
While debating the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027, Hamzah said recent proposals to incorporate elements of the consumption tax into the existing Sales and Service Tax (SST) also indicated that the latter system was lacking.
“If you want the GST, just implement the GST. Don’t leave the people waiting in uncertainty,” Hamzah said.
“This looks like it’s heading in that direction, but no one wants to actually say they want to use the GST.”
He alleged that Pakatan Harapan lawmakers in the government now were “embarrassed” to support reviving the GST due to their rejection of it previously.
First implemented at a standard rate of six per cent in April 2015 under former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, the broad-based consumption tax became a central battleground in Malaysian electoral politics.
Following its historic victory in the 2018 general election, the PH administration zero-rated the GST before repealing it in favour of the current SST regime.

Title: High Court fixes June 14, 2027 for Bar bid to revive Zahid graft case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The High Court today fixed June 14, 2027, for case management of the Malaysian Bar’s judicial review application challenging the prosecution’s decision to discontinue the Yayasan Akalbudi corruption case involving Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Judge S. Indra Nehru set the date after lawyer Abhilaash Subramaniam, representing the Malaysian Bar, informed the court that Ahmad Zahid and the Attorney-General (AG) had obtained leave from the Federal Court on Oct 8 to appeal against an earlier Court of Appeal ruling.
“We therefore request that the judicial review hearing at the High Court be held after the Federal Court appeal proceedings are concluded,” Abhilaash said during case management.
The court also directed that the next case management be conducted via e-review before a High Court deputy registrar.
Abhilaash also informed the court that no date had been fixed for the substantive appeal hearing, adding that preparations, including compiling the appeal records and exchanging written submissions, could take several months.
Federal counsel Safiyyah Omar, representing the AG, agreed to the proposal, while Ahmad Zahid’s lawyer, Datuk Guok Ngek Seong, raised no objection.
On Oct 8, a three-member Federal Court panel led by Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah granted Ahmad Zahid and the AG leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision allowing the Malaysian Bar to initiate judicial review proceedings.
Hashim, sitting with Federal Court judges Datuk Nordin Hassan and Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali, ruled that the case raised novel constitutional questions of public importance requiring clarification and a definitive ruling by the Federal Court.
On May 7, the Court of Appeal granted the Malaysian Bar leave to challenge the AG’s decision on Sept 4, 2023, to discontinue proceedings against Ahmad Zahid.
The appellate court overturned a June 27, 2024, High Court ruling that had dismissed the Malaysian Bar’s application for leave to commence judicial review.
Ahmad Zahid, named as the proposed second respondent in the judicial review, subsequently applied for leave to appeal to the Federal Court on May 25. AG Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar filed a separate application.
In its judicial review application, the Malaysian Bar seeks a High Court declaration that the decision by then High Court judge Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah, now a Federal Court judge, to grant Ahmad Zahid a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) on 47 charges of criminal breach of trust, corruption and money laundering linked to Yayasan Akalbudi was null and void.
The High Court granted the DNAA after the prosecution informed the court that the AG Chambers intended to discontinue the proceedings to examine new evidence. — Bernama

Title: Heavy rain, gusty winds expected across nine states, Putrajaya and Labuan until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning across multiple states, forecasting heavy rain, lightning, and gusty winds in parts of Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, Sabah, and the Federal Territory of Labuan until 6pm today.
The adverse weather advisory, issued at 3pm this afternoon, takes effect ahead of the evening peak traffic hours.
In the northern and eastern regions of the peninsula, the warning encompasses Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, and Selama), Kelantan (Jeli and Gua Musang), and Terengganu (Dungun, Hulu Terengganu, and Kemaman).
Pahang faces widespread exposure across ten districts: Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Jerantut, Bentong, Temerloh, Maran, Kuantan, Pekan, and Rompin.
Further south, the alert covers Hulu Langat and Sepang in Selangor, alongside the Federal Territory of Putrajaya. In Negeri Sembilan, stormy weather is expected across Jelebu, Seremban, Port Dickson, Rembau, and Kuala Pilah.
In Johor, the affected southern corridor includes Kulai, Pontian, Kota Tinggi, and Johor Bahru.
In East Malaysia, the advisory covers northern Sarawak, specifically Limbang and the Bario highlands in Miri.
In Sabah, the warning covers extensive territory across five divisions: Kudat, the West Coast, the Interior (Tambunan, Sipitang, Beaufort, Membakut, Keningau, Tenom, and Kuala Penyu), Tawau (specifically Lahad Datu), and Sandakan (Kinabatangan and Paitan). The Federal Territory of Labuan has also been placed on alert.
MetMalaysia explained that a thunderstorm warning is triggered when cloud formations show signs of imminent heavy rainfall with an intensity exceeding 20 millimetres per hour, or when storms are expected to last for more than an hour.
The department emphasized that these advisories serve as short-term alerts and remain valid for a maximum duration of six hours from the time of issuance.
Members of the public, particularly motorists travelling through affected corridors, are advised to exercise heightened caution on slippery roads, steer clear of flood-prone lowlands, and monitor official meteorological updates for real-time adjustments.

Title: Malaysia urges Umrah pilgrims to hold off travel after deadly Riyadh airport missile strike
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 12 — Malaysians are advised to temporarily postpone travel to Saudi Arabia for Umrah following security concerns after a deadly attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said that while there had been no incident in Makkah, the missile attack in Riyadh had prompted the government to advise Malaysians to defer non-essential travel to Makkah and Madinah for the time being.
“There has been no incident in Makkah, but the missile explosion in Riyadh has raised security concerns,” he told reporters after attending the departure of Jordan’s King Abdullah II at the Bunga Raya Complex here today
Yesterday, the Foreign Ministry reported that no Malaysians had been killed or injured in Saturday’s attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh or the incident involving a projectile that fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation reported that the attack on King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people and injured 309 others.
The fatalities comprised four Saudi nationals, two Bangladeshis and one national each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. — Bernama

Title: Man found electrocuted beside Kota Tinggi TNB substation, cable theft attempt suspected
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Oct 12 — An unidentified man was found  dead early this morning, believed to have been electrocuted while attempting to steal power cables near a Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) substation in Felda Adela, near Sungai Rengit.
The deceased, who carried no identification documents, was discovered sprawled on the road shoulder by members of the public before dawn.
Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said law enforcement was alerted after receiving an emergency call through the MERS 999 response system at 6.46am regarding an unconscious individual.
“Following the information, a police team from the Kota Tinggi district police headquarters were immediately despatched to the scene to investigate.
“Initial checks revealed the male victim lying about a metre away from the TNB substation and about 20 metres from the main road," he said in a statement.
“An examination of the victim’s body found no identification documents or any initial signs indicating foul play,” he added.
Yusof said that investigators combing the scene discovered an assortment of tools suspected to have been used in the attempted cable theft.
“The items found included a small hoe measuring 45 centimetres, a cordless grinder, a steel hammer, a pipe wrench and a headlamp.”
Initial findings suggest the man died from an electric shock while attempting to cut live cabling in the vicinity. Police are currently working to ascertain his identity and confirm the official cause of death.
The body was transported to the Kota Tinggi Hospital forensic unit for a post-mortem, and police have classified the case as a sudden death report.

Title: From Jan 2027, only JPJ‑approved intermediaries can handle customer transactions at counters nationwide
Article:
ARAU, Oct 12 — Only individuals or company representatives registered as intermediaries and approved by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) will be allowed to conduct transactions on behalf of customers at all JPJ offices and branches nationwide from January 1.
JPJ director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the requirement was aimed at regulating intermediary services more systematically, transparently and with integrity.
He said registration as a JPJ-approved intermediary would open on November 1 through an online platform provided by the department.
“Each approved registered intermediary will be issued an official digital identification document bearing a serial number, valid for two years, subject to the department’s terms and regulations,” he told a press conference after inspecting the newly upgraded Perlis JPJ office counters here today.
Aedy Fadly said the implementation did not mean that JPJ had any ties, cooperation or business relationship with any registered intermediary. Registration approval also did not constitute JPJ’s endorsement, recommendation or guarantee of the services offered by the intermediary.
“JPJ will also not be responsible for any losses, fraud, additional charges or disputes arising from private transactions between customers and registered intermediaries.
“In this regard, the public is advised to remain vigilant and prioritise the department’s official channels, such as the MyJPJ application, the JPJ Public Portal, service counters and other official channels provided, to avoid any unwanted risks,” he said.
Aedy Fadly said the initiative reflected JPJ’s continued commitment to strengthening integrity, transparency and service delivery efficiency, while ensuring that customers’ interests remained a priority.
On the upgraded Perlis JPJ counters, he said the office now had a more modern, orderly and conducive environment following upgrading works under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), which were completed in five months against the target of six months.
Aedy Fadly said the improvements were expected to benefit about 400 customers who visited the office daily, while providing staff with a more organised and comfortable working environment. — Bernama
